zip34209.method: ZIP 34209 address points (19,593 from Manatee County GIS General/FeatureServer/5) were sampled (~1,400 addresses spread over every street) and each run through the Supervisor of Elections precinct finder (voterfocus.com PrecinctFinder, county FL-MAN). The personalized sample-ballot PDF for every precinct split found was then downloaded (https://www.voterfocus.com/SampleBallots/WHSampleBallot.php?county=manatee&precinct=<split>&party=GEN&election=245&city=&ward=) and its contest list read. About 170 sampled addresses (mostly long or arterial streets such as Manatee Ave W, 33rd Ave Dr W, Perico Bay Blvd, 59th/60th St W) could not be matched by the lookup and are unresolved, so a few other splits may exist.

candidates.current_office: Sitting Florida House member, District 74 (since 2018), running for the OPEN Senate seat (incumbent Sen. Joe Gruters is term-limited).

2025 state tax package.

votes.what: Lowers the minimum age to buy long guns from 21 to 18 (passed the House; stalled in the Senate).

Expands the state school-voucher program to all K-12 students regardless of income.

candidates.name: Camden "Cam" Bedinghaus
candidates.bio: 23-year-old Manatee County native and district alumnus; USF economics degree (May 2026); served on the USF Campus Council. Director of Turning Point USA Manatee County; journalist at Conservative Coastal News; previously youth coordinator at Bayside Community Church.
candidates.local_ties: Manatee County native who attended Manatee County schools (Bradenton Times; WUSF). Home address not published in sources read. District 5 covers parts of East Manatee including Lakewood Ranch.

record.text: Only District 5 candidate to qualify by petition (signatures) instead of paying the fee.
Primary Aug. 18, 2026: 34.07% (preliminary), second behind Mullis 35.31%; Chantal Wilford 30.62% did not advance.

Platform: declare a reading emergency on day one; early-intervention reading grants; parent portal; financial-literacy program; cut district programs serving fewer than 80% of students and redirect money to progress-based teacher bonuses; on books, says the district should avoid materials he believes could raise student suicide rates.
Has posted on social media about his admiration for Charlie Kirk; says his personal beliefs are conservative but his campaign goals are apolitical.

money_notes.text: About $5,800 raised as of late July 2026 (second among three candidates), mostly individual contributions; contributors include the Tea Party of Manatee County and Vision Source (a business).

controversies.text: Bradenton Times editorial (opinion) describes him as a "social media influencer" with "political/culture-war baggage" that some readers found troubling, and notes his stated commitment to keeping politics and policy separate. No ethics or legal matters found.

endorsements.text: Manatee Patriots; America First Party of Florida; Stand for Health Freedom (WUSF).

candidates.name: Jonathan Mullis
candidates.bio: 49; physical therapist, owner and CEO (with his wife Sonia) of Physical Therapy Doctors of Florida in Bradenton; business owner for about 17 years. Northeastern undergraduate degree and Simmons University doctorate in physical therapy. President of the Bradenton Kiwanis Club; board member of the Manatee Tiger Bay Club.
candidates.local_ties: Bridgewater/Lakewood Ranch resident; moved to Manatee County in 2017 (about nine years) from the Boston area, where he had a practice (Your Observer; Bradenton Times). Daughters attend or attended Manatee School for the Arts, a public charter school in the district. Involved with the Manatee Chamber of Commerce, Lakewood Ranch Business Alliance, and Leadership Manatee.

record.text: Primary Aug. 18, 2026: 35.31% (preliminary), first place.

Platform: expand career and technical education and dual enrollment; volunteer reading mentors/tutors for K-2; pre-K readiness; expand partner-school arrangements; on books, says the district should follow existing state guidelines and its own policies.

money_notes.text: Raised almost $28,000 as of late July 2026 (most of the three candidates). Contributors include Knowledge is Power PAC and several registered businesses such as Ford Drywall & Stucco, Inc.; $150 from Manatee County Commissioner Tal Siddique; $500 from Neil Unruh, identified by WUSF as the county's Chief of Finance.

endorsements.text: The Bradenton Times editorial board recommended him (Sept. 29, 2026; opinion).

candidates.name: Carol Whitmore
candidates.bio: Incumbent Holmes Beach commissioner and current commission chair (chosen 2025). Held offices: Holmes Beach commissioner 1991-98, mayor 1998-2006, Manatee County commissioner (at-large District 6) 2006-2022; elected to the city commission again in 2024.
candidates.local_ties: Said in 2024 that she has lived on the island for 55 years.

votes.what: County board voted 6-1 to remove a 2017 stipulation requiring board approval of the preliminary site plan once 750 units were completed; Whitmore urged a continuance so staff and applicant could agree on clearer language.

record.text: Manatee County commissioner 2006-2022 (chaired the board in 2011); lost the 2022 at-large District 6 Republican primary to Jason Bearden.
Re-elected to Holmes Beach city commission in Nov. 2024 with 1,087 votes (per Anna Maria Island Sun); chosen commission chair in 2025.
Positions stated in Aug. 2024: opposes consolidating the three island city governments; opposes demolishing existing Manatee Beach structures for a three-story parking garage.

2026 questionnaire: main concern is preserving small-town character amid tourism growth; wants better communication between city administration, residents and the commission after the 2024 hurricanes.
In a 2018 county Q&A she said raising millage should be a last resort and that she had never proposed a property tax increase as city mayor.

money_notes.text: 2024 city race: $3,355.80 raised as of July 22, 2024 (the most in the commission race then), including a $1,200 self-loan; named backers included Michael Bennett, Cheri Coryea, Tal Siddique, Darcie Duncan and Bob Carter.
2022 county primary: reported $139,576.03 on hand vs. Bearden $108,303.09 (donors not named in the source).
2026: no new financial activity reported since the July report; no totals stated in the Sept. 1, 2026 article.

controversies.text: June 2022 (county campaign): accused of petit theft over removing an opponent's campaign signs. On Aug. 19, 2022 the State Attorney declined to file charges, stating the State could not prove criminal intent and that Whitmore mistakenly believed two signs were on private property.

measures.name: City of Bradenton Referendum No. 1 - Remove Mayor's tie vote and ex officio council president role; state Mayor is not a council member
measures.summary: Amends the Bradenton City Charter to (1) remove the mayor's right to cast a vote when the council ties, and (2) remove the mayor's designation as 'ex officio president of the Council' and add language that the Mayor is not a member of the City Council. Yes = amend; No = keep current charter.

measures.name: City of Holmes Beach Referendum: vacating a 10-foot alleyway at 2902 Avenue East
measures.summary: Ballot asks whether the City should vacate an unused, inaccessible 10-foot-wide alleyway bisecting the beachfront property at 2902 Avenue E in favor of that property's owner. Yes = vacate, No = deny. A Holmes Beach charter provision requires voter approval for vacations of this kind. The article reports the alley is about 150 feet long and no payment to the city was reported.
measures.who_funds_yes: Not found (no campaign committee reported in sources reviewed). The property owner, Blowfish Island Inc. (managed by Benjamin ten Haff), is the beneficiary and is represented by attorney Garret Barnes.
supporters: Property owner Blowfish Island Inc. via attorney Garret Barnes (bought the lot in 2024 for $7.25 million and plans two homes instead of three)
City Attorney Randy Mora called it a housekeeping action
Holmes Beach commission voted 4-0 on June 23, 2026 (Dan Diggins absent) to adopt Resolution 26-06 placing it on the ballot; the supporting ordinance passed unanimously at two hearings in 2025
opponents: Resident Nancy Deal, the only public commenter, questioned giving up public land; Commissioner Jessica Patel asked whether the city was getting paid. No organized opposition reported in sources reviewed.
measures.gaps: Who funds yes/no not found. Charter basis (supermajority + referendum requirement) not confirmed for this specific alley. An Islander correction states the alley is NOT a beach access path and runs north-south between six privately owned plats; the Sun article reports no payment to the city.

measures.name: Parrish Fire District Referendum: Authorization to Increase Annual Special Assessments for Fire Protection Services
measures.summary: Ballot asks "Shall the Parrish Fire District be authorized to increase its base rate of assessment" by an additional flat $68.00 per developed residential, commercial and industrial parcel per year (vacant, acreage and golf course parcels excluded). Stated purpose: fund additional personnel to move the standard firefighter schedule from 56 to 42 hours per week, consistent with Florida Statutes s. 633.508(7)(c). The assessment is a flat per-parcel charge, not a percentage of property value. Fire Chief Stacey Bailey said shorter schedules support firefighters' mental health and that Florida law encourages the 42-hour policy. Expected total revenue and number of firefighters to be added were not stated in the sources reviewed. Background: the district's 5-year plan says a 2020 referendum to raise the assessment by $80 was approved by voters.
measures.who_funds_yes: Not found (no campaign committee reported in sources reviewed).
supporters: Fire Chief Stacey Bailey (district chief) is quoted supporting the schedule change
opponents: None identified in the sources reviewed (no organized opposition found; not verified that none exists)
measures.gaps: Total revenue, firefighters to be added, and any organized opposition not found. One district Nextdoor post claims an earlier assessment referendum was not approved, conflicting with the 5-year plan's statement that the 2020 $80 measure passed; unresolved.

notes: SCHOOL BOARD vs COMMISSION: the assumption holds for the two districts on the ballot. I took 400 random county address points, got each one's commission district from the county layer (FeatureServer/7) and its real sample ballot from the Supervisor of Elections: of 324 resolvable addresses every commission-District-2 address got School Board District 2 (plus CC2), every commission-District-5 address got School Board District 5, and no address in commission districts 1, 3 or 4 had any school-board race (commission-district-1 addresses saw the CC1 race and no school-board race; districts 3 and 4 saw only the at-large CC6 race; district 2 saw CC2 + SB2; district 5 saw SB5 + CC6). So SB2 = CC2 voters and SB5 = CC5 voters. Only SB2 and SB5 are on the 2026 ballot; I did not test districts 1, 3, 4 (not on ballot). No public school-board polygon layer exists, so use COMMDIST.

ALREADY IN ballot-34221.json (not duplicated): cc1, cc2, cc6, sb2, mosquito, palmetto ward 2, SD20, HD70, HD71, CD16, statewide, retention, Amendments 1-3 and the county GO-bond measure (man-ref-1) and Palmetto charter measure. Of these, a 34209 ballot carries: CD16, SD20, HD71, cc6, mosquito, retention, Amendments 1-3, the county bond measure. cc6 and the mosquito district are countywide (every Manatee ballot).

NEW in this file: man-sd22 (Buchanan/Wasserman/Hyde; not on any 34209 ballot), man-hd72 (Conerly/Shifrin), man-sb5, Holmes Beach mayor/commission/alley referendum, East Manatee Fire Seats 3 and 5, Parrish Fire Seat 1 + referendum, West Manatee Fire Seats 2-4 (ON 34209 ballots), Bradenton Council Wards 3 and 4 + Referenda 1 and 2 (ON 34209 ballots if the voter lives inside the City of Bradenton), 17 CDD/Stewardship seats (names only).

MACHINE FILTER: every race and measure has a 'where' object. For state legislative races I added keys 'sd' and 'hd' (not in your list) with value = the district number; get the voter's SD/HD from TIGERweb layers 1/2 (gis.special.state_legislative_and_congress, CORS tested) or ignore them and show by district. Bradenton Ward 3/4: where={'city':'Bradenton'} only, because every city voter sees both seats (residency wards, citywide vote); the race objects carry 'district':3/4 as the ward. 'kind_machine' = 'race'; the descriptive 'kind' (city/special/STS/STR/school) is kept from the schema; measures carry kind 'measure'. Short labels are <=18 chars.

WEST MANATEE FIRE: the PAO fire layer (gis.special) says which fire district a point is in, but on the actual sample ballots the in-city splits (315.2, 323.3, 323.5, 325.3, 325.4, 327.2, 333.3) had no fire-district race on their sample ballots. Trust the voter's own sample ballot over any inferred layer join.

PRECINCT SPLITS: the personal sample ballot is keyed by precinct split such as 315.2 (not just 315). Precinct finder JSON and the SOE sample ballot PDF URLs are in gis.precincts.note; CORS was not tested and is expected to fail (coordinator already decided to link out).

WEB SEARCH QUOTA: the shared WebSearch budget ran out partway through. Candidate data therefore rests on WebFetch of specific pages: Bradenton Times (opinion pieces labelled as such), city and WMFR sites, county campaign-finance exports (itemized donors, computed by me from voterfocus export.php CSV), Patch ballot guide. Owner-source (Stew Peters / Alex Jones / Rumble Owen) searching is thin: only stewpeters.com/?s=Bradenton was fetched by me (no results); the delegated subagents checked stewpeters.com site search for the SD22/HD72/SB5 names, and rumble/alexjoneslive for a few. Treat 'no mention found' as 'not found in the limited search', not as a clean negative.

SUBAGENT WORK (not independently re-verified by me): races B1 (SD22, HD72, SB5: 10 House roll-call votes each for Buchanan and Conerly from flsenate.gov roll-call PDFs; FL DOE finance site returned 502 so no donor data) and B2 (Holmes Beach, East Manatee/Parrish fire, CDDs; fire candidates are names only, two East Manatee entries flagged unconfirmed identity). Spot-check before relying.

POLLING PLACES: 71 precincts from the SOE directory (https://www.voterfocus.com/PrecinctFinder/precinctDirectory?county=manatee), one place per precinct (not per split). Several churches/buildings host more than one precinct (e.g. River Life Church hosts 113, 219, 221). Voters should confirm with the SOE look-up before going; some elections use a different place.

UNRESOLVED for 34209: about 170 of ~1,570 sampled address-lookups did not match (Manatee Ave W, 33rd Ave Dr W, Perico Bay Blvd, 59th/60th St W areas). The 8 precincts found (311, 313, 315, 317, 323, 325, 327, 333) are consistent in contest content (all carry the same statewide/county/DCA ballot and differ only by city and fire district), so a missed split would only change whether the voter sees West Manatee Fire or the Bradenton contests; a few addresses (Palma Sola Trace, Perico Island, Pointe West) may belong to precinct splits not seen.
